educationalGoal: "Technology Management" is a framework that takes full advantage of technology to develop, maintain, and improve systems, products, and services that are useful for society. In this course, students will understand the mechanisms needed to develop novel value-creation activities, select an appropriate industry and vocation for their abilities, and cultivate motivation toward their chosen area, all while adapting the business organization to the environment.
advice: Points of attention in this course: (1) Students will self-evaluate their achievement during the course. (2) Students are required to understand the contents of textbook prior to class so as to conduct group work in an effective manner. For this purpose, students will utilize textbooks, e-learning tools, and comprehension confirmation quizzes in this course. (3) Group leaders will be evaluated using evaluation sheets that aim to improve their leadership skills and experience. (4) Students will make good use of the study results to develop better career plans. (5) Students will make good use of chapter exercises for further understanding.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Be able to understand the characteristics of a company's management activities and analyze/evaluate the company from the perspectives of management resources, organization, and value creation for customers. (2) Be able to analyze/evaluate study/work from the perspectives of a series of management circles. (3) Be able to understand problem solving by improving quality, cost, and delivery, which represent the value of products, services, and systems, and to resolve problems by referring to cases of actual organizations. (4) Be able to develop a career design plan and explain it to others in a convincing and logical manner.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Be able to understand the characteristics of a company's management activities and analyze/evaluate the company from the perspectives of management resources, organization, and value creation for customers. (2) Be able to analyze/evaluate study/work from the perspectives of a series of management circles. (3) Be able to understand problem solving by improving quality, cost, and delivery, which represent the value of products, services, and systems. (4) Be able to develop a career design plan and explain it to others.
